newsitem.title: USA: Judge's ruling puts Hilton bid on hold.
newsitem.headline: Judge's ruling puts Hilton bid on hold.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp's $6.5 billion takeover bid for ITT Corp was effectively put on hold by a federal judge's denial of a legal motion to force an ITT annual shareholder meeting, analysts said on Tuesday.

Late Monday, U.S. District Judge Philip Pro denied Hilton's legal motion to compel a mid-May shareholder vote on Hilton's offer. ITT will now likely delay the vote until a mid-November meeting, analysts said.
ITT has yet to set the date for the annual gathering, and the ruling gives it until no later than mid-November.
Until a shareholder meeting and vote, Hilton can do little to further its bid except campaign for ITT stockholder votes and waiting to see what ITT's value will be after shedding non-core assets.

"It is a moot issue right now from the standpoint of a tender offer," said Marvin Roffman of Philadelphia-based Roffman Miller Associates. "But Hilton is prepared to go to the end on this thing. They are just not going to stop."
Indeed on Monday, Hilton Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach said the company would to pursue its $55 per share cash and stock offer until it is put to a shareholder vote.
Today, Hilton's senior vice president of corporate affairs, March Grossman, said that philosophy remains intact.

"In a world of uncertainties, the certainty is they are going to have to go in front of shareholders some time and we will be there," Grossman told Reuters. "When we went into this, we were aware it might be a long process and we were prepared for that."
But analysts agreed Hilton's bid will likely change because ITT will be a different company when the offer comes up for a vote.

Since Hilton's late January bid, ITT has sold its stake in French telecommunications company Alcatel Alsthom for about $830 million and agreed to sell its 50 percent stake in Madison Square Garden Inc, owner of the famous New York sports arena and the New York Knicks basketball and Rangers hockey teams, for $650 million.
Analysts said ITT will likely use the money to issue a large shareholder dividend or, more likely, buy back stock. In either case, the structure and value of ITT will change.
Hilton's current tender offer expires on Friday, April 25, and the company will make a decision by then on whether to extend it, Grossman said.
